meta.coverage: Dallas–Fort Worth: North Dallas, Collin County, the East lakes and the West Mid-Cities
meta.method: Editorial profiles written from local knowledge. Scores are 0–5 relative comparisons inside this coverage area, not ratings. Price tiers are relative. Market metrics (median price, inventory, days on market) stay null until loaded from a licensed MLS/market data source.

score_keys.new_construction: Share of newer (2010+) and new-build homes
score_keys.lot_size: Typical lot size; higher means larger lots and acreage
score_keys.amenities: Density of dining, retail and entertainment nearby
score_keys.commute_north: Ease of reaching the Legacy/Plano/Frisco job corridors
score_keys.value: More home for the money; higher means lower relative price

neighborhoods.name: Frisco
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1995–present; active new construction on the north side
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots in master-planned communities; larger lots in select enclaves
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs are the norm, often with amenity centers and pools
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Some newer communities sit in MUD or PID districts that add to the tax rate. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Strong for Legacy/Plano and Frisco job centers. Downtown Dallas is a Tollway drive that is longer at peak hours.
neighborhoods.development: Ongoing mixed-use growth along the Tollway and SH 121, including the PGA of America headquarters at Fields and Universal's family theme park project. Verify current timelines.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Frisco is the default answer for many relocating families: newer homes, big-league sports and entertainment, and a deep bench of master-planned communities with amenity centers.
pros: Entertainment and dining density for a suburb
Close to the Legacy and SH 121 job corridors
cons: Tollway traffic and toll costs to Dallas
MUD/PID districts can raise carrying costs
Pricing is competitive for move-up buyers

neighborhoods.name: West Plano
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1980s–2000s; urban product at Legacy West and Legacy Town Center
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Established suburban lots with mature trees
neighborhoods.hoa: Mix of mandatory and voluntary HOAs; many older sections have light or no HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Established city with no MUD/PID districts in most resale areas. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Next to major corporate campuses at Legacy. The Tollway gives a direct line to Dallas.
neighborhoods.development: Continued corporate and mixed-use activity around Legacy. Verify specific projects before quoting.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Established, centrally located and close to big employers. You get mature neighborhoods without a far-north commute.
pros: Central to North Dallas job centers

neighborhoods.name: Downtown & East Plano
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1960s–1980s single-family; newer infill near downtown
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Modest suburban lots; some larger older lots
neighborhoods.hoa: Many areas have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Established city tax structure. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: US 75 and DART rail from Downtown Plano station give a car-optional path to Richardson and Dallas.
neighborhoods.development: Transit-oriented infill around Downtown Plano station.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: One of the few places in Collin County with a walkable historic downtown and light rail, at a lower entry price than West Plano.
pros: Lower entry price than West Plano

neighborhoods.name: McKinney
neighborhoods.home_age: Historic core (early 1900s) through active new construction to the north and west
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Varied: historic lots downtown, master-planned lots, acreage at the edges
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in newer communities; historic district has preservation rules instead
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Several newer communities sit in MUD/PID districts. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Craig Ranch and the SH 121 side reach Legacy and Frisco easily. The north and east sides mean longer drives to Dallas.
neighborhoods.development: Steady growth along SH 121 and US 380. Watch planned roadway projects on US 380 for commute impact.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: McKinney has a real historic downtown, plus everything from 1900s homes to brand-new master plans. It often gets you more house than Frisco or Allen.
pros: Wide range of price points and home ages
Often more space per dollar than Frisco
cons: Longer commute to Dallas from the north side
MUD/PID taxes in some new communities

neighborhoods.name: Allen
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common, typically moderate dues
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Mostly established resale areas. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: US 75 runs straight to Richardson and Dallas. SH 121 reaches Frisco and Legacy.
neighborhoods.development: Mixed-use along US 75 and SH 121.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Allen is a polished, mid-sized suburb with 1990s–2000s homes, strong retail and a central position on US 75.

neighborhoods.name: Prosper
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Larger-than-typical suburban lots; estate lots common
neighborhoods.hoa: Master-planned HOAs with large amenity packages are common
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Many communities sit in MUD/PID districts. Get the full combined rate before you compare.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Tollway extension access. Frisco is close. Dallas is a long drive.
neighborhoods.development: Major retail and residential build-out along US 380 and the Tollway extension.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Prosper is newer, roomier and more upscale, with big master-planned amenities and a small-town center that is growing fast.
pros: Close to Frisco without its density
cons: Retail still catching up in places

neighborhoods.name: Celina
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Master-planned lots plus rural acreage at the edges
neighborhoods.hoa: Master-planned HOAs (e.g., Light Farms, Mustang Lakes) with large amenity packages
neighborhoods.tax_profile: MUD/PID districts are very common. Compare the total rate, not the base city rate.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Dallas North Tollway extensions are bringing it closer. Today it is a long drive to Dallas and a moderate one to Frisco.
neighborhoods.development: One of the region's fastest-growing cities. Roads, retail and schools are all being built out.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Celina is the far-north frontier: brand-new homes and big amenity communities, for buyers who accept today's drive.
cons: Longest commute to Dallas in this set

neighborhoods.name: Richardson
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1950s–1980s, with newer infill and urban product at CityLine
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Generous mid-century lots with mature trees
neighborhoods.hoa: Many neighborhoods have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Established city tax structure. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: One of the best-connected suburbs. US 75, the Bush Turnpike and several DART stations reach Dallas and Plano.
neighborhoods.development: Corporate campuses at CityLine and transit-oriented development around rail stations. The DART Silver Line adds east-west rail; confirm current service.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Richardson offers mid-century homes on big leafy lots, great transit and quick access to Dallas, at prices below the Collin County new-build belt.
cons: Mixed ISD boundaries; verify by address

neighborhoods.name: Far North Dallas
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots; many townhome and condo communities
neighborhoods.hoa: Varies widely; condos and townhomes carry HOA dues
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas and Dallas County rates. Collin County portions differ, so check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: The Tollway gives a straight shot to Uptown and to Legacy, so it is central for two-job households.
neighborhoods.development: Redevelopment and refreshes around older retail centers.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Far North Dallas is one of the most central addresses for split commutes, with City of Dallas services and a wide mix of housing types.
cons: ISD and county boundaries vary block to block

neighborhoods.name: Preston Hollow
neighborhoods.home_age: Mid-century originals alongside extensive new luxury construction
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Large lots, including some of Dallas's biggest in-city estates
neighborhoods.hoa: Mostly no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas / Dallas County. Taxes scale with high values.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Minutes to Uptown, Downtown and Love Field. One of the shortest luxury commutes in the region.
neighborhoods.development: Ongoing teardown/rebuild of luxury homes and redevelopment around Preston Center.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Preston Hollow means estate lots, luxury new builds and a short drive to everything in central Dallas.
pros: Very short commute to the urban core
cons: Teardown economics drive much of the market

neighborhoods.name: Addison
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Small lots; townhome and urban formats dominate
neighborhoods.hoa: Most townhomes and condos carry HOA dues
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Addison has a notably low city rate. Total tax still depends on ISD and county.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Tollway access, and the DART Silver Line connects east-west. Confirm current service status.
neighborhoods.development: Transit-oriented development planned around the Addison Silver Line station.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: A small town with a big restaurant scene. Lock-and-leave townhomes and condos sit minutes from the Tollway.

neighborhoods.name: Carrollton
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1970s–1990s; newer infill near Downtown Carrollton
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots
neighborhoods.hoa: Many older neighborhoods have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Spans three counties, so rates vary by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Multiple highways plus the DART Green Line, with Silver Line connections at Downtown Carrollton.
neighborhoods.development: Transit-oriented development at Downtown Carrollton station.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Practical, well-connected and less expensive than the Collin County new-build belt, with a rail-served downtown square.
cons: Three counties mean varied tax rates

neighborhoods.name: The Colony
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard lots; lakefront and lake-adjacent options
neighborhoods.hoa: Many older areas have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Denton County rates. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: SH 121 reaches Frisco, Plano and the Legacy corridor quickly. Dallas is a longer drive.
neighborhoods.development: Grandscape's entertainment and retail district continues to expand.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Lake access and Grandscape's entertainment at prices below neighboring Frisco.

neighborhoods.name: Little Elm
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard master-planned lots; lake-adjacent options
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in newer communities
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Some newer communities sit in MUD/PID districts. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Frisco is close. Dallas is a long drive. FM 423 and US 380 get congested.
neighborhoods.development: Lakefront district growth and new subdivisions.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Newer homes near the lake with a beach-town feel and a lower entry price than Frisco next door.

neighborhoods.name: Wylie
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard lots, with larger lots toward Lake Lavon
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in newer communities
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Check by address; some newer areas carry special districts.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: SH 78 and the Bush Turnpike lead to Garland, Richardson and Dallas. The north-corridor job centers are a longer drive.
neighborhoods.development: Steady residential growth on the east side of Collin County.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Small-town feel and newer homes near Lake Lavon at moderate prices.
cons: Far from the Legacy/Frisco job corridors

neighborhoods.name: Murphy
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard to larger suburban lots
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: The Bush Turnpike is close for Richardson and Plano. Legacy is a moderate drive.
neighborhoods.development: Mostly built out; limited new subdivisions.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: A small, quiet suburb of 2000s homes with an east-Plano address feel.
cons: Mixed ISD boundaries; verify by address

neighborhoods.name: Lucas & Fairview
neighborhoods.lot_profile: One acre and up is common in Lucas; Fairview mixes acreage with town-center living
neighborhoods.hoa: Varies; many acreage properties have light or no HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Check by address; some properties may carry agricultural valuations. Verify before purchase.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: US 75 is close for Allen and Plano. Dallas is a moderate-to-long drive.
neighborhoods.development: Limited, low-density growth by design.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Room to breathe: acreage, custom homes and quiet country roads, still close to Allen and Plano.

neighborhoods.name: Anna & Melissa
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard master-planned lots; acreage at the edges
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in new communities
neighborhoods.tax_profile: MUD/PID districts are common in new communities. Compare total rates.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: US 75 south to McKinney, Allen and Plano. Dallas is a long drive.
neighborhoods.development: Rapid builder activity and new retail along US 75.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: The most accessible entry point to new-construction Collin County living, with builder incentives often in play.
pros: Lowest entry price in this set

neighborhoods.name: Princeton
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard master-planned lots
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in new communities
neighborhoods.tax_profile: MUD/PID districts are common. Compare total rates.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: US 380 west to McKinney and US 75. Dallas is a long drive, and US 380 congestion is the main tradeoff.
neighborhoods.development: Very rapid residential growth. Watch planned US 380 improvements.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: New homes at entry prices on the east side of Collin County, for buyers who prioritize space and price over commute.

neighborhoods.name: Rockwall
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard to large lots; lakefront and lake-view options
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in newer communities
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Rockwall County rates. Some newer areas carry special districts, so check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: I-30 runs west across Lake Ray Hubbard into Dallas. Peak-hour bridge traffic is the main tradeoff.
neighborhoods.development: Steady residential and retail growth along I-30 and SH 205.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Lakeside living east of Dallas, with The Harbor's waterfront dining and a small-town square.
cons: I-30 bridge traffic at peak hours
Far from the north job corridors

neighborhoods.name: Rowlett
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard lots; many lake-adjacent streets
neighborhoods.hoa: Mix; many older areas have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Dallas/Rockwall county rates. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: The Bush Turnpike and I-30 reach Dallas and Richardson. The DART Blue Line ends at Downtown Rowlett.
neighborhoods.development: Sapphire Bay, a planned lakefront resort district, has housing built but its resort pieces remain unbuilt. The city issued a notice of default to the developer in January 2026.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Lake-adjacent homes at moderate prices, with a rail line into Dallas.

neighborhoods.name: Garland
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots
neighborhoods.hoa: Many neighborhoods have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Dallas County rates. Garland Power & Light is a city-owned utility, so most residents don't shop for electricity providers.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Several freeways plus DART Blue Line stations reach Dallas and Richardson.
neighborhoods.development: Downtown Garland redevelopment around the square and rail station.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: One of the most affordable places close to Dallas, with rail access and a revitalized downtown.
pros: Lower entry prices close to Dallas
cons: Big city with very different neighborhoods

neighborhoods.name: Grapevine
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard lots; larger lots near the lake
neighborhoods.hoa: Varies; historic areas have preservation rules
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Mostly Tarrant County. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Next to DFW Airport. SH 114 and SH 121 reach Dallas, Las Colinas and Fort Worth. TEXRail runs from Grapevine Main to Fort Worth, and the DART Silver Line serves the airport area.
neighborhoods.development: Ongoing Main Street and lake-area investment; the city brands itself the Christmas Capital of Texas.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: A historic Main Street with wineries and festivals, right next to DFW Airport.

neighborhoods.name: Flower Mound
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Larger lots and preserved open space
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Denton County rates. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Close to DFW Airport and the SH 121 corridor. Dallas is a moderate drive.
neighborhoods.development: Low-density growth guided by the town's master plan.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Spacious, quiet and green, with larger lots and quick airport access.

neighborhoods.name: Las Colinas
neighborhoods.home_age: 1970s master plan to present, with lots of newer urban product
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Small to standard lots; many condo and townhome options
neighborhoods.hoa: Most condos and townhomes have HOA dues
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Dallas County rates. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Central to DFW Airport, Dallas and the corporate offices in the Urban Center. DART's Orange Line serves Las Colinas.
neighborhoods.development: Continued office, hotel and residential growth in the Urban Center.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: A master-planned business district with canals, lakes and lock-and-leave living between Dallas and the airport.
pros: Central between Dallas and the airport

neighborhoods.name: Arlington
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1970s–2000s, with newer areas to the south
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots
neighborhoods.hoa: Mix of HOA and non-HOA neighborhoods
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Tarrant County rates. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Between Dallas and Fort Worth. Arlington uses on-demand rideshare transit (Via) instead of fixed bus routes.
neighborhoods.development: Continued growth around the Entertainment District.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Home of the Cowboys and Rangers: the entertainment capital of the metroplex, centrally placed between Dallas and Fort Worth.

neighborhoods.name: Fort Worth
neighborhoods.home_age: Everything from 1900s historic districts to brand-new suburbs
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Varies widely by neighborhood
neighborhoods.hoa: Varies widely
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Tarrant County rates. Some newer areas carry special districts, so check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Its own job center, with a downtown, medical district and industry. Dallas is a 45-minute-plus drive, so most residents work in Fort Worth.
neighborhoods.development: Large growth across the city, including Panther Island along the Trinity River and new master-planned suburbs.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: A big city with a Western heart: museums, the Stockyards, a lively downtown and neighborhoods at every price point.
cons: New suburbs can be far out
